questions.text: Total Cost of Education Disclosure: Reveal all costs to parents: (1) Tuition fees; (2) Exam fees; (3) Uniform/Book costs; (4) 'Development levies' or PTA fees; (5) Digital device costs; (6) Data consumption estimates (cost to use app); (7) Hidden charges (late fees).
questions.evidence_required: Fee structure document, Data usage estimates, Parent contracts
questions.africa_specific_notes: Hidden fees are rampant. 'Free' education often has many levies. Data cost is a major hidden cost of EdTech.

questions.text: EdTech Subscription Transparency: Clear digital pricing: (1) Freemium limits (what is free vs paid?); (2) Auto-renewal terms; (3) Cancellation process (easy to cancel?); (4) Refund policy; (5) Bundle pricing (with telco data?); (6) Payment methods (mobile money charges?); (7) Trial period terms.
questions.evidence_required: Subscription terms, Cancellation flow screenshots, Payment integration docs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Auto-renewal on mobile money can drain wallets unnoticed. Cancellation must be simple (USSD/SMS).

questions.text: Accreditation Status Disclosure: Prove legitimacy: (1) Registration with Ministry of Education; (2) Exam body accreditation (WAEC, KNEC, etc.); (3) TVET accreditation; (4) University charter status; (5) International recognition (if applicable); (6) Teacher certification status; (7) Expiration of accreditation.
questions.evidence_required: Registration certificates, Accreditation letters, Teacher license list
questions.africa_specific_notes: 'Certificate mills' common. Parents sacrifice to pay fees, need assurance degree is valid. Government registration essential.

questions.text: Curriculum Alignment & Relevance: Explain what is taught: (1) Alignment with National Curriculum (CBC, 8-4-4, etc.); (2) Adaptation for local context; (3) Language of instruction policy; (4) Learning outcomes definition; (5) Skills vs Theory balance; (6) Digital skills inclusion; (7) Update frequency.
questions.evidence_required: Curriculum syllabus, Mapping to national standards, Learning outcome guides
questions.africa_specific_notes: Curriculum changes (e.g., CBC in Kenya) cause confusion. Parents need to know if content helps child pass national exams.

questions.text: Student Data Privacy (Minors): Protect child data: (1) Parental consent mechanism; (2) Data minimization (collect only what's needed); (3) No behavioral advertising to children; (4) Third-party sharing restrictions; (5) Anonymization of research data; (6) Right to delete data (upon graduation/leaving); (7) Compliance with Data Protection Acts.
questions.evidence_required: Privacy policy (child-friendly), Consent forms, Data flow maps
questions.africa_specific_notes: Minors' data highly sensitive. EdTech often monetizes data. Strict consent needed. No ads targeting kids.

questions.text: Algorithmic Grading & Tracking Transparency: Explain AI/Auto-grading: (1) How auto-grading works; (2) Bias testing (language/accent bias in oral apps); (3) Progress tracking logic; (4) Recommendation algorithm (why this lesson next?); (5) Human review option for contested grades; (6) Behavioral tracking (attention monitoring?); (7) Data used for profiling.
questions.evidence_required: Algorithm explanation docs, Bias audit reports, Grading appeal process
questions.africa_specific_notes: AI grading can be biased against African accents/dialects. Parents need to trust the 'machine' grading.

questions.text: Parental Progress Reporting: Keep parents informed: (1) SMS/WhatsApp progress reports (for low-tech parents); (2) Real-time gradebook access; (3) Attendance tracking visibility; (4) Behavior reports; (5) Local language reports; (6) Simple visualizations (traffic lights); (7) Teacher feedback channels.
questions.evidence_required: Report card templates (SMS/App), Parent portal demo, Language options
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many parents illiterate or low-tech. SMS/Voice reports effective. Parents invest heavily, want to see results.

questions.text: School/Provider Performance Transparency: Public accountability: (1) National exam pass rates; (2) University transition rates; (3) Teacher qualification stats; (4) Student-teacher ratios; (5) Infrastructure status (labs, libraries); (6) Safety/Discipline records; (7) Financial audits (for public schools).
questions.evidence_required: Annual performance reports, Exam result summaries, Staffing data
questions.africa_specific_notes: Parents choose schools based on exam results. Transparency drives quality. 'Ghost schools' exist.

scoring_notes: Layer 2 (Transparency) for Education in SSA: Accreditation transparency is the baseline for trust. Pricing transparency (including data costs) is essential for affordability. Data privacy for minors is a growing regulatory focus.
